title: Each water molecule has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom
summary: A water molecule is one unit of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom joined together.
body: OpenStax Chemistry says a molecule is two or more atoms joined by chemical bonds, moving as a unit. A water molecule is the example that contains two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom. Glucose is a different molecule, with six carbon, twelve hydrogen, and six oxygen atoms. The page also says that if a glass of water were enlarged to the size of the Earth, the molecules inside would be about the size of golf balls. The catalog mass of water is a different card and is not repeated here. This card is only which atoms sit in one molecule.
